correctness.rationale: For KG(n,k), n≥3k−1 and k≥2, round-one individualised anchor adjacency makes round-two common-neighbour counts C_A=binom(n−2k+s,k) strictly recover s=|X∩A| and t=|X∩B|. Round-three neighbour moment M=(k−s)(k−t)binom(n−k−2,k−2)+(b−r)binom(n−k−2,k−1) uniquely recovers r=|X∩A∩B|. Ground-set permutations preserving the four regions act transitively on each resulting tuple; any anchored automorphism preserves refinement, proving precise stabilizer orbits. Exact sharpness KG(8,3), |A∩B|=1 gives rounds 3,6,13,14 classes. Independently generated Kneser edges and WL partitions match region profiles for 4 cases, including boundary (5,2).
residual_risks: Finite test instances only; universal statement rests on exact binomial moment proof.

value.rationale: A uniform constant three-round recovery of all two-anchor Kneser point-stabilizer orbits supplies a structural effective refinement lemma relevant to color-refinement complexity and permutation group symmetry. Explicit class sizes and sharp n=8,k=3 witness are natural quantitative information not encoded by generic 1-WL background.
residual_risks: The sharpness example is not a complete parameter-by-parameter optimal-round classification.
